result:
Lowercase comparators like `name like 'Def%'`, `tags.t ilike 'v%'` and `tags.t is null` now work when searching experiments in the database-backed store, and behave the same as their uppercase forms. The experiments test file passes (93 passed, 10 skipped).

**The cause:** `_get_search_experiments_filter_clauses` in `mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py` compared the comparator as typed against uppercase-only lists (`"LIKE"`, `"ILIKE"`, `"IS NULL"`, …). A lowercase comparator didn't match any of them and was rejected with the "Invalid comparator" error. Searching runs and traces in the same file already uppercases the comparator first, which is why those worked.

**The fix:** the function now uppercases the comparator (`f["comparator"].upper()`) before any checks. Every later check and the SQL it builds see the normalized value, so experiment names, other attributes and tags are all covered. Experiment searches go through this one function whether or not workspaces are enabled. Uppercase input is unchanged.

**The test:** I added `test_search_experiments_lowercase_comparators` in `tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_experiments.py`. It checks lowercase `like`/`ilike` on experiment names and on tags, plus `is null`/`is not null` on tags. It runs with workspaces both on and off. With the fix temporarily removed, it fails with `Invalid comparator 'like'`; with the fix in place, it passes.
